short: A Gothic army destroyed the eastern field army and killed an emperor, opening the frontier for good.
full:
Gothic groups fleeing the Huns had been admitted into the empire in 376 under terms Roman officials then abused, driving them to revolt. On 9 August 378, the eastern emperor Valens attacked a Gothic camp near Adrianople without waiting for reinforcements from his western co-emperor Gratian. Gothic cavalry, returning from foraging, struck the Roman flank as infantry battle was joined, encircling and destroying most of the Roman army.

Valens himself died on the field, his body never recovered, and roughly two-thirds of the eastern field army was lost in a single afternoon, among the worst defeats in Roman history. The empire could no longer expel the Goths by force and instead settled them within its borders as semi-autonomous federates under their own leaders, a precedent that permanently changed how Rome absorbed and depended on barbarian manpower for its remaining armies.
